overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by giving insufficient notice of the May 13, 2019 executive session topic and by failing to name the bargaining units when convening in executive session on February 4 and May 13, 2019; no further relief ordered beyond future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the February 4 and May 6, 2019 notices lacked specificity by not naming the collective bargaining units in the PEC bargaining executive session topic.
allegations.key_passage: We conclude that the February 4 and May 6, 2019, meeting notices were sufficiently detailed

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the May 13, 2019 notice's executive session topic on PEC collective bargaining did not identify the bargaining units to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: the May 13, 2019, notice was not sufficiently detailed as it failed to identify the collective bargaining units to be discussed

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the chair failed to announce the specific bargaining units before convening in executive session on February 4 and May 13, 2019.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements (no additional relief ordered for the procedural violation because the executive session minutes were released).
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
